title: SAVE Studie-SArcoma Surgery with Vacuum Enhanced wound treatment Randomised controlled Study to evaluate the wound management in sarcoma surgery
summary: The study is a multicentre trial in which the effect of a vacuum therapy on wound complication after resection of sarcomas is examined. To achieve that, the particiants get a primary suture or a vacuum therapy decided by chance after the surgery.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other connective and soft tissue

interventions.name: Control Group: Primary Closure after Resection of Sarcoma
Intervention Group: Vacuum-Therapy after sarcoma resection with secondary wound closure

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients must be over 18 years old.
- Patients of any gender and background 
- The largest tumor diameter on imaging must be at least 5 cm. Preoperative imaging is required to assess tumor dimensions.
- Sarcomas must be located in the lower extremity or groin.
- Cases must be discussed preoperatively at an interdisciplinary tumor board.
- Patients must provide informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
- Tumors smaller than 5 cm and superficial masses.
- Patients with local recurrences or prior wound healing complications in the surgical area.
- Patients with ulcerating or infected tumors, or those requiring emergency surgery.
- Other Soft Tissue Tumors such as Kaposi sarcoma.
- When direct closure is not possible during the initial surgery due to the extent of resection.
